```{r}
library(tidyverse)
```

## Load the data
```{r}
epss_now <- read_csv(here::here("data/raw/epss/epss_scores-2026-10-27.csv.gz"), skip = 1)
```

## 1. Basic Checks
```{r}
glimpse(epss_now)
summary(epss_now)
```

## 2. Spread of scores
```{r}
epss_now |>
  ggplot(aes(x = epss)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(title = "Most CVEs are very unlikely to be exploited: the median EPSS score is 0.6%",
       x = "EPSS score (log scale)", y = "Number of CVEs")
```
EPSS scores 396,257 CVEs (including ones older than 2016). The median score is 0.0063, so half of all CVEs have under a 0.63% chance of being exploited in the next 30 days. 62.6% score under 1%, and only 4.4% score 10% or more. That is why the x-axis is on a log scale: on a normal scale almost every CVE would sit in one bar at zero.

## 3. Exploited vs. not exploited
```{r}
v <- readRDS(here::here("data/processed/vulns.rds")) |>
  left_join(epss_now |> transmute(cve_id = cve, epss_now = epss), by = "cve_id")

v |>
  group_by(exploited) |>
  summarise(n = n(), median_epss = median(epss_now, na.rm = TRUE))
```

```{r}
ggplot(v, aes(x = exploited, y = epss_now)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(title = "Exploited CVEs score about 100 times higher on EPSS today",
       x = "In KEV (exploited)", y = "EPSS score today (log scale)")
```

## 4. CVEs with no EPSS score on 1 January 2025
```{r}
v |> count(no_score_2025 = is.na(epss_2025_01_01),
           published_2025_or_later = published >= as_date("2025-01-01"))
```
Exploited CVEs have a median EPSS score of 0.49 today, against 0.0049 for the rest: about 100 times higher. Part of this gap is circular, because EPSS raises a score once exploitation is seen, so today's score is not a fair prediction test. That is why the model in Phase 3 uses the 1 January 2025 snapshot instead.

134,243 CVEs had no EPSS score on 1 January 2025, but 133,746 of them were simply published after that date. Only 497 older CVEs were missing a score, and none of them were exploited.

## Findings

1. The median EPSS score is 0.0063: half of all CVEs have under a 0.63% chance of exploitation in the next 30 days, and only 4.4% score 10% or more.
2. Exploited CVEs score about 100 times higher today (median 0.49 vs 0.0049), though today's score partly reflects exploitation already seen.
3. Almost every CVE published before 2025 had an EPSS score on 1 January 2025; only 497 did not.
